newsitem.title: USA: Young blames stock drop on Merrill report.
newsitem.headline: Young blames stock drop on Merrill report.

text.p: Young Broadcasting Inc on Thursday blamed the sharp decline in its share price yesterday on a Merrill Lynch report that raised red flags about advertising revenue at its Los Angeles television station.
In the report, issued Wednesday morning, Merrill also lowered its rating on Young to "neutral" from "accumulate."
Young's stock fell five points yesterday to 22-1/4, a 52-week low. About 2.4 million shares changed hands, compared with a daily average of some 82,000.
In morning trading today Young's stock was up 1-5/8 to 23-3/4. About 400,000 shares had been traded by mid-morning.

Young did not say if the issues raised in the Merrill report were valid, and did not say how its earnings could be affected by any drop in advertising revenues at KCAL-TV, its independent station in Los Angeles.
The company could not be reached for further comment.
